Parameter Description: Type of Selection

Source: R/parameter_descriptions.R
param_typeOfSelection.Rd

Parameter Description: Type of Selection

Arguments

typeOfSelection

Rule for selecting treatment arms (multi-arm designs) or populations (enrichment designs) for continuation after an interim analysis. The default "best" selects only the single best arm or population; "rBest" (also accepted as "rbest") selects the best rValue; "epsilon" selects those within epsilonValue of the best; "all" retains all remaining arms or populations; and "userDefined" applies selectArmsFunction or selectPopulationsFunction. Selection is applied at interims with adaptations = TRUE. See the section Treatment arm and population selection for details and an example of gradual elimination.

Treatment arm and population selection

Selection determines which treatment arms or populations continue to the next stage. It is applied at interim analysis k only if adaptations[k] = TRUE; the default enables selection at every interim. Otherwise, the current selection is retained. Once dropped, an arm or population cannot be selected again. In multi-arm designs, these rules apply to the active treatment arms; the control group is retained.

The ranking uses the cumulative interim data and the criterion specified by effectMeasure: the estimated treatment effect for "effectEstimate" (the default), or the test statistic for "testStatistic". The selection functions use a vector effectVector on a scale where larger values rank better. For survival endpoints with effectMeasure = "effectEstimate", this is the estimated hazard ratio for directionUpper = TRUE and its reciprocal for directionUpper = FALSE.

"best" (default)

Selects only the single best remaining arm or population. Thus, with three active arms and selection enabled at the first interim, only one arm continues to stage 2. It does not drop just the worst arm. If several have the same best value, the first in the original order is selected.

"rBest"

Selects the rValue highest-ranked remaining arms or populations, subject to availability. Specify rValue as a positive integer. For example, rValue = 2 selects the best two; rValue = 1 gives the same selection as "best". The same rValue is used at every enabled interim, so this option does not mean dropping one arm or population at each interim. The spelling "rbest" is also accepted.

"epsilon"

Selects the best and all other remaining arms or populations whose selection value is at most epsilonValue below the best value, including equality. Specify epsilonValue on the scale of effectVector. The number selected depends on the observed differences and can vary between simulation runs. For example, selection values c(0.20, 0.35, 0.40) and epsilonValue = 0.10 retain the second and third arms or populations. For response-rate differences, 0.10 represents 10 percentage points.

"all"

Retains all remaining arms or populations without ranking them. This disables dropping based on relative performance, but threshold conditions and stopping rules still apply.

"userDefined"

Uses selectArmsFunction in multi-arm designs or selectPopulationsFunction in enrichment designs. Supply a function returning a logical vector in the original arm or population order, with TRUE indicating selection. Its length must equal the original number of active arms or populations. The function can use stage, effectVector, and the other arguments listed in the corresponding parameter description. Use this option for rules whose number selected changes by stage, such as dropping the worst remaining arm at each interim.

For the four built-in rules, selected arms or populations must additionally have a selection value strictly above threshold. The default threshold = -Inf imposes no additional restriction. Consequently, fewer than the requested number may continue, or none may continue. For "userDefined", implement any threshold condition in the supplied function. Efficacy and futility stopping rules apply separately from selection.

For example, the following multi-arm selection function drops one worst remaining arm at each enabled interim, while retaining at least one arm. Pass it as selectArmsFunction = dropWorstArm together with typeOfSelection = "userDefined". If three arms are still available at the first interim, it retains two; at the next enabled interim it retains one, provided the trial continues.


dropWorstArm <- function(effectVector, selectedArms, stage) {
    keep <- selectedArms[seq_along(effectVector), stage] & !is.na(effectVector)
    if (sum(keep) > 1L) {
        remaining <- which(keep)
        worst <- remaining[which.min(effectVector[remaining])]
        keep[worst] <- FALSE
    }
    keep
}
